record.what_it_does: Meta's Marketing API and hosted MCP server for managing and reporting on Facebook/Instagram ads.
record.auth_notes: Facebook Login (for Business) OAuth gives user access tokens with ads_read and/or ads_management scopes. Business Manager system users can generate long-lived tokens for server-to-server automation on business-owned assets. These are static bearer tokens, and they can't attribute actions to a real end user unless that user goes through Facebook Login. The Meta-hosted ads MCP server supports three auth methods: OAuth via Facebook Login for Business, a user access token, and a system user access token. Tokens are sent as an Authorization: Bearer header.
record.access_notes: Creating a Meta app and adding the Marketing API product is free. Limited (formerly Standard) access is granted automatically and works for ad accounts you own or manage. Apps that manage other people's ad accounts need Advanced (Full) access to ads_read/ads_management, granted per permission through App Review. Business Verification is also tied to accessing sensitive data. Using the hosted MCP server does not require owning a Meta app. Bringing your own app (to set the OAuth client ID) means adding the 'Create & manage ads with ads MCP server' use case. There is no paid plan; the API is free to use.
record.api_breadth_notes: The Graph API-based Marketing API covers ad accounts, campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, insights/reporting, custom audiences, catalogs, pixels/Conversions API, system users, ads webhooks and sandbox ad accounts. Well over 50 operations.
record.mcp_notes: Meta-hosted remote MCP at https://mcp.facebook.com/ads, announced on the Meta developers blog on 2026-07-16. Its tool categories are reporting, ad creation/management, catalogs, signals/datasets, help and troubleshooting, A/B tests and conversion lift studies, and activity logs. Auth is OAuth (Facebook Login for Business), a user access token, or a system user token. Owning a Meta app is not required. If you use your own app, you pass the app ID as the OAuth client ID and must match the redirect URL. The community server pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp also exists.
record.blocker_notes: A multi-tenant toolkit that serves other users' ad accounts needs Advanced access to ads_read/ads_management through App Review, and likely Business Verification. Development against your own accounts, or against a sandbox ad account, works immediately at Limited access. The getting-started page for the hosted MCP doesn't mention App Review. Meta's MCP blog says Advanced Access for your own app is requested under Permissions and features, then App Review.
